STILL OPEN: 2048 -> 384 = 3/16, i.e. >>2 to the raw/64 scale then x0.75; the 0.75 lives after 0x0208253C, unread.

P211-read the formula tail and mapped the damage model END TO END. Runtime traced a flat -512 term (2.0 in 8.8, which is why every scan for 128 in raw/64 units missed it for 14+ iterations -- a real and important unit mismatch). BUT THE TERM IS NOT CONSTANT: 0x02082644 lsleq r4,r5,#6 then 0x0208264C subeq r0,r0,r4,asr #8 is r0 -= (r5<<6)>>8 = r5/4, i.e. 25% OF THE BASE. r5 was 2048 on their run so r5/4 = 512 exactly, and their measurement cannot separate flat from proportional. DISAMBIGUATING TEST SENT: DOWN+B (base byte 7, base 1792) gives 320 = 5.000 under flat and 336 = 5.250 under proportional; the doc's row says 5.000. One certified DOWN+B run decides it, no deck needed. TWO GATES, both reading the SAME byte table 0x02092E68 (both pool loads resolve to 0x0208269C): gate 1 at 0x02082634 fires when table[r1] == 1; gate 2 at 0x02082650 needs bit 5 of r2 = [r8+0x40] AND table[r1] == 2. Table values: [0]=1 [1]=1 [2..7]=2, so an index maps to a damage CLASS and total reduction is 0%, 25% or 50%. FULL CHAIN: base = ldrsb [elem+0x10+4] (measured 8); r3 = base<<8 = 2048; x [attacker_scratch+0x184]/256; x [attacker_scratch+0x186]/256; x nature_table[defence][attack]; minus r5/4 per gate; out = (r5+r0)>>2 written at 0x02082684 str r1,[fp]. CORRECTED A MISREAD in their trace: r3 going 4 -> 262144 at 0x02082644 is the RESULT FLAG WORD being built (orreq r3,r6,#4 then lsleq #0x10, bit 2 = resisted, returned via r6 at 0x02082648 and r0 at 0x02082680), not a damage value -- so 'the source of that 2 is the per-target resistance' has no referent. WHY THE ABILITY POKES DID NOTHING: the reduction is gated on a flag bit and a class table, not on the ability bitset, so an ability must feed those flags at LOAD time -- the derived-value hypothesis. NEXT TARGET: whatever sets bit 5 of [r8+0x40].

P212-WROTE THE HANDOFF for 201-212 (five cycles overdue) with the damage formula SOLVED. Runtime's certified measurement at TWO bases, control firing twice each, confirms PROPORTIONAL: B base 2048 subtracted 512, DOWN+B base 1792 subtracted 448, both exactly base/4, ratio constant at 0.750. My static decode and their measurement agree -> CROSS_CONFIRMED. THEIR FLAT READING IS RETRACTED and they verified my encodings from arm9.bin before running (0x02082644 = 0x01A04305 moveq r4,r5,lsl #6; 0x0208264C = 0x00400444 subeq r0,r0,r4,asr #8). DOC REFUTED: Damage-Reduction-Is-Flat.md's central claim (constant difference, non-constant ratio) is wrong. Its DOWN+B row of 5.000 is a bad measurement -- the certified value is 5.250 -- and the method is invalidated too, because DOWN+B forces an opponent CHARACTER SWITCH so the HP word afterwards belongs to a different character (runtime measured the delta going UP by +0.578). The doc noted neither move was side-effect-free without realising that was fatal to its own HP-dip oracle. AND MY P182 INSTINCT WAS RIGHT ALL ALONG -- I wrote '0.750 is a clean 3/4, look for a multiply' and abandoned it because the doc's second row implied a non-constant ratio. The row was wrong. A bad measurement in the record killed a correct hypothesis for about thirty iterations.

confirmed_constants.player_slot_0x558_list: a node list walked by 0x0207871C: `ldr ip,[r0,#0x558]; cmp ip,#0; bxeq lr; ldrb r2,[ip,#0x40]`. Nodes carry a byte at +0x40. Battle_Add calls it TWICE per slot, with r1 = 0 (0x0214D89A) and r1 = 1 (0x0214D8B4), so the walk is mode-flagged.
confirmed_constants.player_slot_0x21C_is_not_a_field: guard 8 reports +0x21C as address-taken, but it is the first half of the stride computation (`add r1,r4,#0x21c` then `add r4,r1,#0x400` = 0x61C). An address-taken hit inside a constructor's clearing loop may be loop arithmetic, not structure.
confirmed_constants.sp_total: player_slot+0x5C8 IS THE SP TOTAL -- 11 accesses, the most of any slot field. SP-apply 0x020781E4(r0=slot, r1=amount): if amount >= 0 take the unguarded path (bge 0x207824c); else read the signed byte at slot+0x5CF (`add r0,r4,#0x500; ldrsb r0,[r0,#0xcf]`) and RETURN if non-zero; otherwise `ldr r0,[r4,#0x5c8]; add r0,r0,r1; str r0,[r4,#0x5c8]`. So the guard blocks LOSS but never GAIN. Reachable from a character as [[char+0x1b4]+0x5C8] -- deck-wide SP.
confirmed_constants.eight_bit_offset_split_rule: ldrsb/ldrsh/strh (and ldrh) carry only an 8-BIT offset, so any offset above +0xFF is split as `add rD,base,#0x500` then a small immediate. An ad-hoc offset scan of ComicDeck.cpp reported 0xA0/0xCC/0xCD/0xCF/0xDA/0xE0-0xE3/0xF0-0xFC -- ALL PHANTOM; the real fields are 0x500 higher. struct_fields.py's guard 9 resolves this; ad-hoc scans do not.

confirmed_constants.deck_node_walker_halving: 0x0207871C(r0=slot, r1=mode) over slot+0x558: skip if node+0x40 != 0; if (node+0x0F & 0x10) == 0 OR mode == 0 then node+0x3C |= 0x5000 and node+0x18 = 0; else node+0x3C &= ~0x1000, |= 0x4000, and node+0x18 = node+0x16 / 2 with round-toward-zero (`add r2,r2,r2,lsr #31; asr r2,r2,#1`). Battle_Add runs it twice per slot, mode 0 then mode 1.
confirmed_constants.deck_node_walker_abort: 0x020785B8(r0=slot, r1) over slot+0x558: loads 0x64 into r4 before the loop; per node reads node+0x3C and if bit 0x2000 is set RETURNS from the whole walk (popne), else clears 0x1000 and reads node+0x40. Contrast with +0x40, which skips only the current node.
confirmed_constants.deck_node_0x3C_bits: 0x1000 cleared by both walkers; 0x2000 tested by 0x020785B8 and aborts the traversal; 0x4000 set on the halving path; 0x5000 (= 0x4000|0x1000) set on the zeroing path.
confirmed_constants.deck_add_entry: 0x02076E38(r0=slot, r1=id, r2=a, r3=b, [sp+0x28]=c, [sp+0x2c]=d) -- ADD ENTRY TO DECK. Returns 0x20000000 if the free list slot+0x560 is empty; 0x40000000 if an active node is a DUPLICATE (walks slot+0x558, reads [node+0x34], compares its first halfword to id); 0x10000000 if 0x02076D30(slot,id,a,b) returns 0; bails if 0x02076C98(slot,id) returns 0. On success: unlink(slot+0x560, node); link(slot+0x558, node) -- reached as `add r0,sl,#0x158` then `#0x400`, a split immediate; memset(node+0x0C,0,4); memset(node+0x10,0,0x22); node+0x0C = id (strh); node+0x0E = (a & 0xF) | ((b & 0xF) << 4).
confirmed_constants.deck_node_0x34: points at the entry's DATA RECORD, whose FIRST HALFWORD is the entry ID -- used by the duplicate check at 0x02076E68-0x02076E78. Deck entries are UNIQUE BY ID.
confirmed_constants.deck_list_roles_confirmed: +0x560 FREE and +0x558 ACTIVE, now seen from both directions: construction links every node onto +0x560 (iteration 106), and the add function unlinks from +0x560 and links to +0x558 in one body (0x02076EE0-0x02076EF4).
confirmed_constants.deck_id_lookup: 0x02076C98(r0, r1=id): returns 0 for id == -1, id < 0, or id >= [deck+0x18EC]; otherwise returns [deck+0x30] + id*0xC. So the deck's ID TABLE is at deck+0x30 with 0xC-BYTE ENTRIES and its COUNT at deck+0x18EC. Four callers.
confirmed_constants.deck_add_validator: 0x02076D30(r0=deck, r1=id, r2=a, r3=b): fails if a >= 5, fails if b >= 4, then requires 0x02076C98(deck,id) != 0; then calls 0x02076D00 and reads [result+0x14], extracting FOUR 5-BIT FIELDS (bits 0-4, 5-9, 10-14, 15-19, each and #0x1f) ORed into one mask, then `lsl r1,r1,r5` (shifted by a). a and b are exactly the two nibbles packed into node+0x0E by the add.
confirmed_constants.0x0214BD80_is_the_comicdeck_block: CORRECTS an earlier note that called it a 'chr_b base ptr'. 0x0207602C loads the address and 0x02076038 does `str r0,[r3]`, storing the 0x1914 ComicDeck allocation. 97 literal loads ROM-wide. The block is therefore reachable BOTH from this global and from root+0x114. Immediately after, `ldr r0,[r7]; add r8,r0,#0x64; mov r4,#4` walks the four player slots -- an independent confirmation of the slot count.
confirmed_constants.deck_header_fields: +0x30 = ID table base (0xC-byte entries); +0x38 = second table base (0x18-byte stride, used by 0x02076D00 which indexes it with two signed bytes from its argument's +0x8/+0x9); +0x18EC = the +0x30 table's entry count. +0x30 and +0x38 lie inside the 0x58 header iteration 106 left unexplained.
confirmed_constants.deck_node_0x34_source: node+0x34 = the ID-table entry pointer. In add-entry 0x02076E38: `bl 0x02076C98` then `movs r5,r0` at 0x02076EB8, and `str r5,[r4,#0x34]` at 0x02076F3C. So r5 = [deck+0x30] + id*0xC. This is why the duplicate check (iteration 108) works by reading [node+0x34] and comparing its FIRST HALFWORD to the id -- table entries carry their own id.
confirmed_constants.deck_tables_are_runtime: BLOCKED by the static-only constraint. deck+0x30 (the ID table base) has NO word store anywhere in ComicDeck.cpp 0x02075FBC-0x02078D00; deck+0x38 is set from a VIRTUAL CALL's return (`ldr r2,[r0]; ldr r2,[r2,#0x2c]; blx r2` at 0x020760D8-0x020760E0, stored at 0x020760EC); deck+0x18EC (the count) is never written in the module. The deck's static data is loaded at runtime, so the tables are not at any computable ROM address.
confirmed_constants.deck_entry_construction_chain: validate (a<5, b<4, id resolves) -> r5 = [deck+0x30] + id*0xC -> unlink a node from slot+0x560 -> link to slot+0x558 -> memset(node+0x0C,0,4) and memset(node+0x10,0,0x22) -> node+0x0C = id, node+0x0E = (a&0xF)|((b&0xF)<<4), node+0x34 = r5.

confirmed_constants.deck_global_ov6_holder: battle code holds the deck global in exactly ONE place: ov6 0x0215FAC4 (load at 0x0215FAEC) -- the function that calls the character view's reset 0x0215FB88 and issues selector 5. The only direct battle->deck reach is inside the view/CharaInfo path.
confirmed_constants.deck_0x30_writer_not_a_holder: no word store to +0x30 exists in any of the 55 holder functions (the only hit was `str [r13,#0x30]`, a stack store in 0x020790F0). So whoever fills the ID table base RECEIVES THE DECK AS AN ARGUMENT rather than fetching the global.
confirmed_constants.pc_relative_load_mask: the correct test for `ldr rD,[pc,#imm]` is mask 0x0FFF0000 compare 0x059F0000. Using mask 0x0F7F0000 CLEARS THE U BIT so a 0x059F0000 compare can never match -- it silently reports zero hits.
confirmed_constants.shared_encoding_decoders: struct_fields.py now exports is_bl(x), is_ldr_pc(x) -> (rD, signed disp), is_mov_imm(x) -> (rD, value). Selftest verifies each against a hand-read instruction AND a case it must reject: is_ldr_pc accepts 0x02076CB4 -> (0, 0x20) and rejects the non-pc load 0x02076CC0; is_mov_imm rejects the CONDITIONAL movlo at 0x02076CD0; is_bl accepts 0x02076EB4 -> 0x02076C98 and rejects the bxeq at 0x02076CA4. USE THESE instead of writing a mask inline.
confirmed_constants.comicdeck_block_zeroed: ComicDeckCreate does memset(deck, 0, 0x1914) at 0x0207603C (size from the literal [0x020763B4] = 0x1914), immediately after storing the block into the global at 0x02076038. So deck+0x30 (ID table base) and deck+0x18EC (its count) both START AT ZERO.
confirmed_constants.deck_table_fields_have_no_identified_wri: 0 word stores to +0x30 among the 55 deck-global holders; 0 stores ROM-wide resolving to +0x18EC via the add+str split (0x18EC exceeds a 12-bit immediate so it must be split). confirmed_constants.deck_add_entry_is_dead: FIFTH VESTIGIAL SYSTEM. Four independent routes to a deck pointer were enumerated and NONE writes deck+0x30: (1) the global 0x0214BD80 in ARM -- 0 of 55 holder functions; (2) one call hop from a holder -- 1 hit of 79 callees, and it is Battle_ColObjCreate 0x0207AEDC writing its OWN +0x30 on a 0x40-byte ColObj; (3) THUMB -- zero pc-relative loads of 0x0214BD80 anywhere in the ROM, so the 375 thumb `str [rN,#0x30]` sites cannot reach a deck; (4) root+0x114 -- 21 sites in 17 functions, none stores +0x30. Combined with memset(deck,0,0x1914) at creation and 0 add+str pairs reaching +0x18EC, the count stays 0, 0x02076C98 rejects every id, 0x02076D30 fails, and 0x02076E38 always returns 0x10000000. The 16-node array, both lists, the unique-by-ID rule and both walkers never run.

confirmed_constants.deck_dead_residual: unswept: register-offset stores, stm, and ARM call chains beyond one hop.
confirmed_constants.dead_deck_residual_closed: Across the 72 functions that can hold a deck pointer (55 global holders + 17 root+0x114 readers) there are exactly 7 register-offset stores and 2 stm. confirmed_constants.scaled_register_split: THIRD split form in this ROM, after add-then-immediate and the 8-bit ldrsb offsets: `add rD, base, rI, lsl #n` then `[rD, #imm]`. This is an ARRAY at offset imm with element size 1<<n, and its EXTENT comes from the guarding cmp on the index. struct_fields.py's guard 9 handles a constant add only, which is why KomaList+0x14 is absent from its field map.
confirmed_constants.struct_fields_guard_12: SCALED-REGISTER ARRAYS. `add rD, base, rI, lsl #n` then `[rD, #imm]` is an array at +imm with element size 1<<n; the extent comes from a `cmp rI, #N` searched in a window either side of the add. CRITICAL: these adds are frequently CONDITIONAL (addne/addeq, the arms of an optional copy), so the guard must NOT require cond == AL. Selftest asserts KomaList+0x14 reports array[6]x0x4. Effect on existing maps: KomaList 11 -> 12; ColPrm record and ov6 battle character unchanged (genuine null result -- no scaled arrays in their anchors).
confirmed_constants.split_forms_handled: FOUR forms now: (9) `add rD,base,#N` then `[rD,#M]`; (10) 8-bit offsets on ldrsb/ldrsh/strh via effective_offset; (11) `add rD,base,#N` then a strided walk; (12) `add rD,base,rI,lsl #n` then `[rD,#imm]`. Not claimed that a fifth does not exist.

HP_UNITS_CORRECTION: HP is a u16 LITTLE-ENDIAN in 1/64 units. The "1/4 scale byte" in older docs is only the HIGH BYTE. Read 2 bytes at addr, not 1. Naruto 4-koma = 9216 raw = 144.0. Goku 10240 = 160.0. Luffy 9728 = 152.0. Anything reading one byte silently truncates - distrust prior sub-integer damage conclusions. Sizes 7-8 coming from a different chr_b entry also explains the komatxt rename to ナルト（九尾）, and 208 matches "8-koma have the most HP".
hp_findings.WEAKNESS: Only 19/74 entries are non-decreasing across the five slots (e.g. chr_b[66]=[104,64,152,64,224]). Either (A) slots are per-size HP but only the sizes a character owns are meaningful and the rest is filler, or (B) my stride-4 grouping is wrong and I am reading one byte from each of five different fields that happen to share the multiple-of-8 property. Reading these as u16 gives high bytes 1,4,5,16,20,22 (not constant), which favours B for the field boundaries. Confidence PLAUSIBLE, not confirmed.
hp_findings.FALSIFIABLE: Naruto size-5 panel (koma.bin record 502): mine says 160 (raw 10240), harness says 152 (raw 9728), my old guess said 180 (dead). One exact u16 read decides between two live hypotheses.

HP_SOLVED.formula: max_HP = chr_b[index][size-4] + 8 * (active Ｊ魂+ sources). index = koma.bin byte 0x7 (abilityId) for battle panels. Per-size array = five u8 slots at 0x10/0x14/0x18/0x1C/0x20 (stride 4) indexed by size-4. Battle sizes are 4-8 = exactly five slots.
HP_SOLVED.verified: Harness cross-checked 6 populated RAM deck slots against chr_b[index][0]: six for six, with +8 on exactly the two ACTIVE characters and 0 on the four benched. Battle struct carries the chr_b index at hp_addr + 0x29.
HP_SOLVED.F1_ANSWER: Naruto size-5 = 160 displayed = raw 10240. My iteration-7 prediction CONFIRMED. Both size*36 (180) and 8*(14+size) (152) REFUTED.
HP_SOLVED.filler_resolved: Iteration-7 reading (A) is CORRECT. Of 370 slots only 174 are meaningful (one per character+owned-size pair); the other 196 are filler, which is exactly why 55/74 entries looked non-monotonic. Example: chr_b[0] 悟空 owns sizes 4-5 = [152,168,168,168,168], and RAM showed Goku active at 160 = 152+8.
HP_SOLVED.192_208_attribution: Both true. chr_b[12] = [144,160,176,192,208] is a complete ladder for a character owning all five sizes. chr_b[24] = [80,96,112,192,208] and is reached ONLY by koma records 504/505 (both ナルト（九尾）, sizes 7-8), so its slots 3-4 really are Naruto size-7/8 HP. HP values are shared across characters so identical arrays are common.
caveats: Cannot separate "is leader" from "is currently active" - both actives had exactly one +8 source. The +8 is confirmed, its trigger is not.
slot->size rests on the structural argument plus one observed anchor (Naruto size4=144); sizes 5-8 not yet observed in RAM.
These are MAX HP. Damage arithmetic uses 1/64 raw units but stored HP carries no fraction.

RETIRED_METHOD: Poking ability IDs does NOT work. Harness ran a controlled negative: removing 0x09 from Luffy and adding 0x09 to Goku both left damage exactly unchanged, with three controls (poke provably reaches memory, edit persists across attacks, both directions tested). The runtime ability array is a READ-ONLY SOURCE LIST; resistance is precomputed at character load. So card E1 could never have worked by poking - closing it statically was the only route. "Write an ID and observe" is retired for all future cards.

overlays.CRITICAL_FOR_WATCHPOINTS: ov00-ov09 ALL load at 0x0214CD20 - mutually exclusive, one per game mode. A RAM address in that window means different things in different modes. ov10/ov11 at 0x02172A60, ov12/ov13 at 0x021AC1C0.

nature_P1b_REFUTED: Nature is NOT a per-koma-indexed table anywhere in the ROM binaries. Exhaustive: every byte offset, 3 encodings (u8 / nibble / 2-bit), across arm9.bin + all 26 bin/ files + all 14 overlays. Zero candidates. Constraint used: all 312 helper indices must share one value (owner: helpers are always なし) AND the 578 non-helpers must hold >=3 other values each appearing >=50 times.
nature_REFRAME: Deck-System.md says nature variants REUSE the same battle data and specials still use the base nature. So panel nature is NOT a combat property - it is deck-building only, used for deck bonuses. That means it need not sit near chr_b/chr_s at all, and only has to exist where the deck editor + deck-bonus calc run: the deckmake overlay data, or inside the .aar archives that only that mode loads.
nature_remaining_ranked: 1. Inside the .aar archives - InfoDeck.aar (570KB, ~130 entries) is the koma-browser data with a working parser (Binary2InfoDeckDeck); its NON-STRING fields have never been examined. Also deckmake.aar, Deck.aar.
2. The deckmake overlay static data (now extractable, overlay not yet identified)
3. Computed at load time - harness proved resistance is precomputed at character load; nature may be too, in which case no table exists and only load-path disassembly finds it.
METHOD_NOTE: THE GROUP IS THE SIGNATURE, NOT THE ELEMENT. My first nature scan used Naruto 9-panel nature pattern -> 224 candidates, all noise (in 2-bit data only 4 values exist so a 9-element equality pattern matches constantly). The 312-way invariant dropped it to zero. Harness hit the identical lesson in RAM: a single 0x50 slot matched 1167 times in 4MB, four consecutive slots at stride 0x50 was unique. A wide invariant beats a clever pattern.
ADDRESSES_ARE_SESSION_LOCAL: CRITICAL: absolute battle addresses shift between sessions - harness saw the player array at 0x021DF1D4 in one battle and 0x021DF1B4 in another (0x20 shift, same deck). Fails SILENTLY: the stale address returned 62072 from an unrelated array whose neighbours decremented by a tidy 48. Always discover via scripts/emu/find_battle_structs.py. Slot structure (portable): HP u16 +0x00, ability count +0x02, ability IDs +0x03, chr_b index +0x29, slot stride 0x50. CORRECTED 2026-08-14: +0x61C (player->opponent) IS valid after all - the earlier warning was the peer applying it to a stale base from a different session. GDB gave both structs directly: player 0x021df19c, opponent 0x021df7b8, difference exactly 0x61C, and struct +0x18 = HP confirmed live. The scanner base equals struct+0x18. In that savestate opponent HP was at 0x021DF7D0, NOT 0x021DF7F0 - watching the latter was reading garbage, which is what made the opponent side look flat. Human-Testing-Queue.md header updated with this warning.
leader_vs_active_still_open: Harness tried 3 routes, all dead ends: (1) touching the in-battle koma grid never switches the active chr_b index (touch injection itself verified working), (2) poking HP to 0 cannot force a KO because training regen outruns the death check, (3) J Arena index 2 is local wireless multiplayer not vs-CPU - ランキング (index 0) is the vs-CPU ladder and is the right target. "+8 on the active character" now reproduces across two sessions.
nature_P1c_REFUTED: The compacted 578-entry model (non-helpers only, koma-index order) is ALSO refuted: 578-byte windows with exactly 3-4 distinct values each appearing >=80 times, u8 encoding, across all 26 bin/ files + 14 overlays + arm9.bin. Zero candidates.
PERF_NOTE: Sliding-window scans over these files: use a ROLLING HISTOGRAM (add entering byte, drop leaving byte) for O(n). The naive O(offsets x window) version got killed before finishing; the rolling version completes in seconds.

nature_P1d_PLAUSIBLE.model: panel nature = character BASE nature (chr_b/chr_s offset 0x00), OVERRIDDEN on panels whose koma.bin flags byte 0xB has bit 0x10 CLEAR
nature_P1d_PLAUSIBLE.why_it_explains_the_refutations: Only 26 panels need an override; the other 864 inherit from the character. That is exactly why no per-koma nature table exists anywhere (P1b/P1c exhaustively refuted).
nature_P1d_PLAUSIBLE.base_nature_candidate: chr_b.bin offset 0x00 = {0:35, 1:22, 2:17} (74 entries); chr_s.bin offset 0x00 = {0:63, 1:67, 2:63} (193 entries). Both exactly 3-valued = 力/知/笑 with なし excluded (helpers have no entry in either file). Support split is near-perfectly even. Naruto chr_b[20], 九尾 chr_b[24] and 悟空 chr_b[0] all read 0 and all three are 力 characters, consistent with 0=力 but 3 same-value samples cannot prove the mapping.
nature_P1d_PLAUSIBLE.alt_flag_CONFIRMED_MEANING: koma.bin byte 0xB bit 0x10 CLEAR marks the ALTERNATE of a same-size pair. 26 panels total (flags 0x00 x9, 0x01 x3, 0x20 x11, 0x21 x2, 0x42 x1); 25 of 26 pair with a same-character same-size sibling; 25 of the 33 duplicated-size groups have exactly ONE member alt-flagged. Naruto 笑 size-4 = koma record 501 is alt-flagged, its 力 sibling 500 is not.
nature_P1d_PLAUSIBLE.THE_ONE_MISSING_PIECE: What the override RESOLVES TO. Naruto base=0 and his alternate shows 笑. If 0=力,1=知,2=笑 then that is base+2 mod 3, but one sample cannot separate "+2 mod 3" from "always 笑" from "a 26-entry lookup".
nature_P1d_PLAUSIBLE.cheapest_test: ONE data point from a character whose base nature is NOT 力. If a 知 character alternate is 力, the rule is base+2 mod 3 (each nature alternates to the one it loses to). If every alternate is 笑 regardless of base, it is a constant. 22 battle characters read 1 at offset 0x00 and 17 read 2 - those are the discriminating ones.

HP_byte_CONFIRMED_BY_INSTRUCTION: 0x02077C50: ldrb lr,[r4,#0x10] ; lsl lr,lr,#6 ; strh lr,[r1,#0x16] (max) ; strh lr,[r1,#0x18] (current). So HP init literally reads the BYTE at chr_b record +0x10 and shifts left 6 (x64). My table offset and the 1/64 scale are now CODE FACTS, not inferences.

runtime_battle_struct.note: 0x02077DA4 does current += [+0x49]*2 clamped to max, matching the measured ~64 raw per ~2 frames if rate=32. So 自己回復 and the training auto-heal share this machinery and the mode selects the rate.

NATURE_SOLVED.ENUM: 0 = 力 Power, 1 = 知 Knowledge, 2 = 笑 Laughter, 3 = なし Neutral
NATURE_SOLVED.RULE: helper (panelType 2) -> 3. battle (panelType 0) -> nib=(flags>>4)&0xF; nature=nib if nib!=3 else chr_b[abilityId*60 + 0x00]. support (panelType 1) -> chr_s[abilityId*20 + (kshapeGroup-1)*8].
NATURE_SOLVED.KEY_TRICK: 3 in the high nibble is a NO-OVERRIDE SENTINEL, not a value. Nature is COMPUTED, not stored - which is why no value-space search over files could ever find it.
NATURE_SOLVED.VERIFIED: All 9 of Naruto koma 497-505 reproduce the owner observed table exactly (9/9).
NATURE_SOLVED.distribution: 890 panels: 力 226, 知 183, 笑 169, なし 312. battle(206): 力96/知57/笑53. support(372): 力130/知126/笑116. helper(312): all なし. Only 32 battle panels carry an explicit override (nibbles {0:12,1:7,2:13}); all supports and helpers are nibble 3.
NATURE_SOLVED.corollary: chr_s offsets 0x00 AND 0x08 are per-size nature slots (support path indexes (kshapeGroup-1)*8), which is why offset 0x00 showed a near-even 3-way split - it was one of two nature columns.

MY_ERRORS_CORRECTED: Iteration 4 "nature is not in koma.bin" was WRONG. I argued Naruto size-2 (笑) and size-3 (力) were byte-identical except image/shape/ordinal, so no field could encode nature. The error was DISMISSING THE DIFFERING FIELDS: kshapeGroup differs and is a lookup input. Lesson: "the differing fields are incidental" is a claim needing evidence, not a default.

Iterations 9-10 "exhaustively REFUTED" was OVERSTATED. The searches were sound and there is no DEDICATED table, but they only tested dedicated tables (byte/nibble/2-bit at every offset). They never tested a nibble of an existing field plus sentinel-and-fallback. The word "exhaustive" claimed more coverage than the method had.

Iteration 10 P1d mechanism REFUTED: the test is high-nibble==3, not bit 0x10 clear. My bit test caught nibbles 0 and 2 (25 records) and missed nibble 1 (7 records) - close for the wrong reason. 32 override panels, not 26. The SHAPE of P1d (base + override) was right.
METHOD_LESSON: Static value search found every TABLE in this system (sizes, shapes, footprints, types, abilities, names, HP) and then failed on the one property that is a FUNCTION. Two of natures three inputs (panelType, kshapeGroup) were fields already decoded for other purposes. No value-space search can find a computation. What cracked it: the peer overlay-residency test told me WHICH overlay to read, then reading the accessor.

combat_phase_entry_points.scope: combat code = arm9.bin + overlay ov06 ONLY (byte-verified resident). bl 0x020783CC appears 8x in ov06, 0x in arm9.bin.
combat_phase_entry_points.nature_in_combat: RESOLVED, and it is NOT the multiplier. 0x021540AA (ov06, Thumb) calls the nature predicate 0x02078CB8 purely to choose an ASSET FILENAME: predicate true -> "battle/chr/??_?_??_b.aar" with VRAM allowance 0x005F2000; false -> "battle/chr/??_?_??.aar" with 0x005F1000. So a panel with an explicit nature override loads the _b sprite archive - correct for the alternate-nature variants having different art. No damage arithmetic at the site. This is the ONLY use of the predicate in ov06 (confirmed by my own Thumb-aware scan). See docs/research/findings/c0-nature-in-battle.md
combat_phase_entry_points.damage_apply: 0x02078488 core (HP = clamp(current+delta,0,max)); public entry 0x020783CC; list variant 0x020783DC. 8 call sites in ov06 listed in state. Delta arrives ALREADY COMPUTED, so resistance is upstream - trace the producers of r1.
combat_phase_entry_points.method_note: Static value search finds TABLES. It cannot find FUNCTIONS. Reach for disassembly sooner in this phase - the koma sprint lost several iterations to that lesson.
combat_phase_entry_points.MY_ERROR_4: "In arm9.bin" does NOT mean "runs in this mode". arm9 is always-resident and mode-agnostic; only the CALLER identifies the mode. Use scripts/find_callers.py (peer) BEFORE assuming a function participates in a phase.
combat_phase_entry_points.METHOD_LESSON_SHARPENED: Value-space search cannot find a computation, AND text-grep cannot find an ABSENCE. "Zero callers" is only meaningful once you have the COMPLETE binary set - grepping the 9 dumped disasm files would have missed it, and overlays sharing a load address make "which file is this in?" ambiguous. The absence of a caller is as informative as the presence of one.
combat_phase_entry_points.damage_dispatcher: All 8 ov06 sites are handlers in a script-effect dispatcher shaped: ldr r1,[r1,#4] (effect record); ldrsh r1,[r1,#4] (signed halfword data parameter); lsl r1,r1,#6 (x64, displayed->raw); bl 0x020783CC. So damage values are AUTHORED IN DISPLAYED UNITS and scaled at the last moment. A sibling at 0x02159290 uses lsl #8 into a different stat - a family of "apply data parameter to stat X" handlers. NONE of the 8 contains resistance math; it is upstream in hit resolution, still not found.
combat_phase_entry_points.sub_integer_damage_discriminator: The measured 1.250 damage = 80 raw is NOT a multiple of 64, so it did NOT come through a lsl #6 handler. At least one damage path produces a genuine sub-integer value. Useful discriminator for locating that path.
combat_phase_entry_points.THREE_WAY_EPISTEMIC_NOTE: Worth keeping straight, because two separate things were wrong and they cancelled: (1) MY PREMISE WAS INVALID - "the function is in arm9.bin, therefore it runs in this mode" is not valid reasoning; arm9 is always-resident and mode-agnostic, and only the caller identifies the mode. (2) MY CONCLUSION WAS NONETHELESS CORRECT - nature really is read in ov06. (3) THE REFUTATION WAS ALSO WRONG - it rested on a BL decoder that handled only ARM (0xEB) and missed Thumb BL/BLX, so it manufactured a confident "zero callers in ov06". Do not collapse this into "my reasoning was fine after all". The reasoning was bad and the answer was lucky. Both facts stay on the record.
combat_phase_entry_points.LESSON_absence_claims: An ABSENCE claim silently inherits every gap in the method behind it. "Zero callers" is only as strong as the decoder is complete - and an absence is exactly the kind of claim a teammate propagates without re-verifying. What exposed the gap was a live GDB breakpoint capturing lr = 0x02150ddd: bit 0 set means the caller was THUMB. Treat all pre-fc56df9 caller counts from the peer as ARM-only until re-run.
combat_phase_entry_points.damage_bypass_SUGGESTIVE_NOT_PROVEN: Across 14736 breakpoint hits on the HP-apply function 0x02078488, EVERY delta was +128 (+2.0 displayed) from one Thumb caller - the training auto-heal, once per character per frame. ZERO negative deltas. BUT the peer could not confirm a melee hit landed during that window (the constant per-frame heal pins HP at max, so a damage dip is invisible), so this is SUGGESTIVE that melee damage bypasses 0x02078488, not proof.
combat_phase_entry_points.HP_APPLY_HAS_14_CALLERS_NOT_8: My Thumb-aware scan found SIX Thumb blx callers of 0x020783CC that the earlier ARM-only list missed: 0x02150DD8, 0x021513D8, 0x021513EE, 0x021514E6, 0x021515B2, 0x02151636 - plus the 8 known ARM sites. All 14 in ov06, none elsewhere. VALIDATED AGAINST HARDWARE: the peer GDB captured lr = 0x02150ddd, and my thumb-blx at 0x02150DD8 has return address 0x02150DDC | 1 = 0x02150DDD. Exact match, so 0x02150DD8 is the training auto-heal caller they hit 14736 times.
combat_phase_entry_points.melee_damage_lead: The FIVE remaining new Thumb sites (0x021513D8, 0x021513EE, 0x021514E6, 0x021515B2, 0x02151636) are the best candidates for melee damage. The peer 14736-hit observation saw deltas from only ONE caller and suggested melee bypasses 0x02078488; a simpler explanation is that melee comes through one of these five previously-unknown sites and none fired because no melee hit landed in that window.
combat_phase_entry_points.TRIANGLE_CONFIRMED_IN_CODE: 0x02160944-0x021609B8 (ov06, ARM) loops over characters comparing nature at runtime struct +0x13 via chain [r2]->+0x118->+0x56C. Pairs tested: (mine 0, theirs 2), (mine 1, theirs 0), (mine 2, theirs 1) - i.e. every pair is "theirs beats mine" under Power>Knowledge>Laughter>Power. This CONFIRMS FROM INSTRUCTIONS both the enum mapping 0=力/1=知/2=笑 and the triangle direction. It accumulates a COUNT into [r7,#0x60], so it is a counter not a multiplier. Likely consumer: the SP-gain passive "increase SP vs opposing nature" (owner category 36), a deck-level nature bonus, or an AI heuristic. Whoever reads [r7,#0x60] settles it.
combat_phase_entry_points.nature_read_sites_unexamined: Nature is read at 10 sites in ov06 via struct +0x13. Two clusters explained; still unexamined: 0x021548F4, 0x0215DD7C, 0x0215F594, 0x02160260, 0x02163DFC, 0x021672D8

DENOMINATOR.deviation_from_plan: The plan said bucket functions by ADDRESS RANGE. That cannot work: ten overlays load at 0x0214CD20, so range-bucketing would multiply-count every overlay function. functions.json already has a provenance field naming the source binary, so I attribute by provenance and use address ranges only as a consistency check (which passes - no function falls outside its claimed window).

DENOMINATOR.CRITICAL_LIMITATION: The call graph in functions.json is INTRA-BINARY ONLY. Of 13809 caller edges, ZERO cross a binary boundary. Ground truth proving the gap: 0x020783CC (HP-delta apply) has 8 callers all in ov6 (harness verified by decoding BL across every binary), functions.json records none of them AND does not list that address as a function at all. Consequence: caller/callee data CANNOT establish which mode uses an arm9 function. This is the SAME blind spot that produced my "in arm9 therefore runs in battle" error. Any "which mode calls this?" question needs a cross-binary call graph built by decoding BL out of the binaries - not by grepping the text disassembly, which only covers the files someone dumped.
DENOMINATOR.next_tool_worth_building: A cross-binary call graph over arm9 + all 14 overlays would give the real combat denominator and fix the connectivity blind spot. The harness peer has scripts/find_callers.py which does this for a given address list; scaling it to all 8712 functions is the obvious follow-up.

C6_PARTIAL.what_the_8_ARM_sites_are: Cases in ONE dispatcher, all identical: ldr r0,[r5,#0x1B4] (target pointer); mov r1,r4 (delta); bl 0x020783CC; b <switch exit>. So r5+0x1B4 is the target and r4 is the delta, set up BEFORE the switch rather than per-case.
C6_PARTIAL.WHY_IT_IS_A_DEAD_END_HERE: Every write to r4 in the enclosing function: ldr r4,[r0,#0x8] at 0x0215795C, ldr r4,[r0,#0x18] at 0x021579EC, and mov r4,r3 at 0x02157A4C. The last means THE DELTA IS A FUNCTION ARGUMENT - the dispatcher receives an already-computed number and routes it. So move damage is NOT tabulated at these sites and C6 as scoped CANNOT produce a table. The value is computed by this dispatcher CALLER, one level up.
C6_PARTIAL.the_record_read_is_elsewhere: The peer ldrsh r1,[r1,#4] observation must be at one of the six sites I did not decode, not these two.
C6_PARTIAL.VERIFICATION_TARGET: Goku B = 6.000 (384 raw), DOWN+B = 5.000 (320 raw) against an ability-free target. UP+B is a MULTI-HIT string (1.0, 2.0, 1.0, 1.0), so any table must distinguish per-hit values from string totals - several records or a repeat count. Damage is authored in DISPLAYED units (apply sites do lsl #6), so a real table should hold literal 6 and 5.
C6_PARTIAL.OVER_FIT_I_BACKED_OUT_OF: The four u16s at chr_b +0x30..+0x36 looked like base+0,1,2,3 (Naruto 362-365, Luffy 536-539). Across all 74: only 15 sequential, 8 all-zero, 51 NEITHER (Goku is 337,0,338,0). So they are four independent IDs that happen to be contiguous for some characters. Failed to match the non-zero count to owned panel sizes. Recorded as an unresolved field, not a pattern.

C6b_STATUS_OPCODES.FINDING: ov06 has a family of script-opcode handlers sharing the prologue push{...}; mov r2,#ID; ...; bl 0x0215986C (validator). Nine found, and their opcode IDs are EXACTLY the status-effect enum 0x19-0x22.
C6b_STATUS_OPCODES.handlers: 0x19@0x02159694 shock, 0x1A@0x02159678 freeze, 0x1B@0x02159624 burn, 0x1C@0x02159538 confusion, 0x1D@0x02159500 poison, 0x1E@0x02159594 judgment, 0x1F@0x021594E4 paralysis, 0x20 NOT FOUND (blindness - different prologue shape), 0x21@0x02159578 speed-down, 0x22@0x02159608 seal
C6b_STATUS_OPCODES.THE_KEY_RESULT: Only TWO handlers touch HP: 0x1B (burn) and 0x1D (poison) - exactly the two damage-over-time statuses. So the record-reading "damage" sites are STATUS TICKS, not melee. The mapping was not fitted: 0x19-0x22 came from Cheat-Code-Analysis.md ability IDs much earlier, and the handler IDs landed in the same range independently.
C6b_STATUS_OPCODES.one_ID_space: Status effect N is applied by opcode N, and ability N grants immunity to status N. One ID space, both directions.
C6b_STATUS_OPCODES.poison_handler_read: ldr r1,[r4,#0x4] (node->[4] = effect record); ldr r0,[r5,#0x1B4] (target); ldrsh r1,[r1,#0x4] (delta = SIGNED halfword at record+4, so the same field can express a heal); bl 0x020783CC.
C6b_STATUS_OPCODES.caller_tally: 6 Thumb = heals; 2 ARM = poison/burn ticks; 6 ARM still unclassified. NO MELEE DAMAGE among any caller identified so far.
C6b_STATUS_OPCODES.not_established: Two other sites read the same ldrsh ...,#4 shape (0x02159274, 0x021592D0) but sit in functions my prologue scan did not classify - possibly a sibling family (different target, or SP rather than HP). Not claimed.

C6c.ALL_14_CALLERS_CLASSIFIED: 6 Thumb heals (regen +128, full heal 16384); 2 ARM status ticks (poison 0x1D, burn 0x1B, value from an effect record); 2 ARM thin script wrappers (displayed / raw units); 3 ARM larger dispatchers receiving the delta as a function argument; 1 ARM accumulator flush. NONE is a melee-specific site.
C6c.THE_ACCUMULATOR: Inside the per-character state dispatcher 0x02159EF8: 0x0215A300 ldr r0,[r6,#0x1A8]; ldr r0,[r0,#0x10]; ldr r1,[r0,#0x140] (pending HP delta); cmp r1,#0; beq skip; ldr r0,[r6,#0x1B4] (target); bl 0x020783CC. Then the same shape for +0x144 -> 0x020781E4 (SP). So [char+0x1A8]->+0x10->+0x140 is a PENDING HP CHANGE flushed once per dispatcher pass and skipped when zero; +0x144 is the SP equivalent.
C6c.why_it_reconciles_everything: It explains why the harness found the delta always arriving PRE-COMPUTED at the apply sites - it is read out of an accumulator something else filled in. Best candidate yet for the melee path.
C6c.hitbox_priority_link: 0x02159EF8 is exactly the function Battle-Engine-Map claim 4 flagged as "architecturally the right neighborhood for clash resolution" (SPECULATIVE, no two-entity comparison found). There is now a CONCRETE MECHANISM inside it. Claim 4 stays SPECULATIVE - the writer is not found - but it has something to hang on. Whoever writes +0x140 is the damage producer, and that write is where the flat -2 resistance must be applied.
C6c.thin_wrapper_family: Five siblings, all (context,node) -> signed halfword at node->[4]->[4] -> apply: 0x02159260 lsl#6 displayed -> HP; 0x02159280 raw -> (unresolved); 0x021592A0 lsl#6 displayed -> 0x020783DC the ALL-LIVING-CHARACTERS variant; 0x021592C0 raw -> HP; 0x021592DC raw -> SP. So the script VM has separate opcodes for HP/SP, displayed/raw, single/all. The value is SIGNED so one opcode covers damage and healing.
C6c.SP_APPLY_IDENTIFIED: 0x020781E4 is the SP-apply sibling of 0x020783CC. 19 call sites, and they sit IMMEDIATELY AFTER HP-apply sites (0x02157DD0 after 0x02157DC0, 0x021582D4 after 0x021582C4, 0x02158BCC after 0x02158BC0, 0x0215A334 after 0x0215A318) - handlers apply an HP delta and an SP delta as a pair.

WATCH_TARGET_FOR_HARNESS: [character + 0x1A8] -> +0x10 -> +0x140 as a WORD, watched per frame. On a landed melee hit it should go non-zero for one frame then return to zero as the dispatcher consumes it. Much better than breakpointing the shared apply function because it isolates melee from the heal spam and the script opcodes. If it stays zero through a hit that visibly reduces HP, this is refuted.
ACCUMULATOR_LEVEL_CORRECTION: The peer could not resolve +0x1A8 (null everywhere) because of a LEVEL ERROR in how I described the chain. Confirmed statically: 0x020783CC is a 2-instruction thunk - ldr r12,[pc,#4] (=0x02078488); ldr r0,[r0,#0x56C]; bx r12 - and 0x02078488 takes the CHAR STRUCT (ldrsh r2,[r0,#0x18]). So the real chain is: r6 --+0x1B4--> E (entity) --+0x56C--> char struct --+0x18--> HP, while r6 --+0x1A8--> obj --+0x10--> obj2 --+0x140--> pending HP delta. +0x1A8 and +0x1B4 belong to r6, ONE LEVEL ABOVE the entity. Their E candidates were correct; they read +0x1A8 off E instead of off r6.
HOW_TO_FIND_r6: r6 is the first argument (0x02159EF8 opens push{...}; mov r6,r0). BUT 0x02159EF8 has ZERO direct BL/BLX callers across arm9 and all 14 overlays, so it is invoked through a function-pointer table (consistent with a state-machine dispatcher) - there is no call site to read the argument from. Find it by STRUCTURE: locate an E, scan RAM for words equal to E, take r6 = location - 0x1B4, then confirm against r6 other fields: +0x14 halfword flags (the function first act is ldrh r0,[r6,#0x14]; tst r0,#1), +0x1A0 pointer, +0x1A8 pointer to the accumulator chain, +0x1B4 pointer to E. Two-field agreement is the check.

HP_WRITER_SET_COMPLETE.method: Constrained scan: strh [rN,#0x18] requiring a ldrsh [SAME rN,#0x16] within +/-8 instructions (a real HP writer must read max HP to clamp). Requiring the SAME BASE REGISTER is what ties both accesses to one struct. 226 sites -> 17.
HP_WRITER_SET_COMPLETE.ov6_result: Exactly ONE ov6 hit, 0x02160738, and it is a SERIALISER not damage - every field from +0xE to +0x1C goes through the same transform (bl 0x0200D12C signed / 0x0200D338 unsigned) with [r9+0x4E] as a mode byte. The "clamp read" my filter matched was just +0x16 taking its turn. SO THERE IS NO MELEE-SPECIFIC HP WRITER IN THE BATTLE OVERLAY.
HP_WRITER_SET_COMPLETE.the_8_functions: All 17 constrained hits resolve to 8 arm9 functions: 0x020772E4 (0 ov6 callers), 0x02077768 (0), 0x02077C0C (0), 0x02077CB8 (0), 0x02077D40 (0, 6 write sites = the regen family), 0x02078428 (2), 0x020785B8 (1), 0x02078660 (NINE).
HP_WRITER_SET_COMPLETE.core_apply_is_a_mid_function_entry: 0x02078428 CONTAINS 0x02078488, so the core apply is a mid-function entry point, not a function start. That is why the thunk has 14 callers while the enclosing function has only 2.
HP_WRITER_SET_COMPLETE.THE_NEW_LEAD: 0x02078660 has 9 ov6 call sites never examined: 0x02150516, 0x02150592, 0x02150906 (Thumb), 0x02157D44, 0x0215AC4C, 0x0215CAA8, 0x0215CAF0, 0x0215CCE8, 0x0215CE40. Plus 0x020785B8 (multiplicative, smulbb) has one at 0x0215CBEC.
HP_WRITER_SET_COMPLETE.plus_0x558_list: BOTH unexamined functions open ldr rX,[r0,#0x558] and walk a node list, checking a byte flag at node +0x40 and bit-testing a word at node +0x3C. The list-variant apply 0x020783DC also opens ldr r4,[r0,#0x558]. Battle-Engine-Map already names +0x558 as "the Meter-node list, the leading candidate" for guard/SP gauges (campaign item B12, DONE) - so this is a KNOWN structure used by HP-modifying code nobody had connected to it. A list walk is a plausible melee mechanism (a hitbox can strike several entities). SPECULATIVE - I have not read the 9 call sites, and a +0x558 walker with a divide-by-100 could equally be a meter routine, which is what B12 concluded.

METHOD_NOTE_third_time: Two of three scans this session produced confident false positives from OFFSET-ONLY matching (+0x18 -> 226 hits; +0x140 -> a vtable initialiser). The constrained version cut 226 to 17 and was STILL wrong about its single ov6 hit - but wrong in a way I could SEE, because 17 sites are readable and 226 are not. C4_PHYSICS_IS_AN_ARRAY.FINDING: ov11 (battle AI) function 0x0217E4A0 writes THREE IDENTICAL 5-field groups on base r5 at stride 0xC: records at +0x58, +0x64, +0x70, each laid out +0x0 word, +0x4 half, +0x6 half, +0x8 half, +0xA byte, from the same source registers (r12, r2, r1, r3, r11) in the same order. That is an array, not three coincidences.
C4_PHYSICS_IS_AN_ARRAY.ALL_GDB_OFFSETS_FALL_INSIDE: +0x6A = record1 field +0x6; +0x6C = rec1 +0x8; +0x72 = rec2 +0x2; +0x74 = rec2 +0x4; +0x7A = rec2 +0xA; +0x7C = RECORD 3 +0x0 (so >=4 records). The 2026-02-03 GDB session read them as three 16-bit PAIRS at 8-byte spacing; they are different fields of different records at 12-byte spacing. The observation was real, the framing was not.
C4_PHYSICS_IS_AN_ARRAY.why_round1_failed: There is no single X/Y velocity offset to find. That explains the failure better than the documented tool gaps (though those are real - search-imm genuinely cannot see register-indexed stores).
C4_PHYSICS_IS_AN_ARRAY.second_array: The +0x98-0xBA "timer region" offsets (+0x98, +0xA0, +0xA8, +0xB0, +0xB8) are STRIDE 8 - a second array, of 8-byte records. The session even guessed "32-bit values read as 16-bit?", the right instinct aimed at the wrong structure.
C4_PHYSICS_IS_AN_ARRAY.confidence: CONFIRMED_STATIC that +0x58..+0x7A is three 12-byte records with that layout. PLAUSIBLE that it is the same struct GDB observed (all six observed offsets land inside, but r5 identity not proven). UNKNOWN what the records mean - the ov11 function writes the SAME values to all three, so it is initialising/broadcasting, which reveals layout not meaning. Candidates: per-limb hitbox state, a position/velocity history ring, per-hit records. DELIBERATELY NOT naming them velocity fields - that guess produced four demoted claims in round 1.

INCONCLUSIVE_TEST_recorded: Before that, I tried to prove the physics and HP offsets share a struct by finding a function touching both on the same base register. Function-scoped, PC-relative excluded: 65 hits, many with base r13 (the STACK POINTER - locals, not a struct). Useless, and the FOURTH time this session the same failure: +0x18, +0x6C, +0x78 are commonplace so co-occurrence proves nothing. What worked was the opposite move - not "do these offsets co-occur?" but "do these offsets have STRUCTURE?". Stride-12 repetition is self-evidencing in a way co-occurrence never is.

DAMAGE_FIELD_FOUND.THE_MISS: There are TWO trampolines into the HP apply. 0x020783CC is plain. 0x020783B8 is a DRAIN that does rsb r1,r1,#0x0 - it NEGATES the delta, so a caller subtracting HP passes a POSITIVE magnitude. I enumerated the 14 callers of the plain trampoline and correctly found only heals/status/dispatchers, because DAMAGE DOES NOT USE THAT TRAMPOLINE. The drain has only 2 callers and I never looked.
DAMAGE_FIELD_FOUND.THE_FIELD: 0x0215AC70 calls the drain trampoline with r4 loaded at 0x0215AC08 from ldr r4,[r1,#0x134], where r1 = [r5+0x1A8] -> +0x10 - the SAME chain as the +0x140 heal field. So that object holds a family of pending deltas: +0x134 HP damage (positive, negated by the drain), +0x138 SP drain (negated by rsb), +0x140 HP heal (plain trampoline), +0x144 SP add.
DAMAGE_FIELD_FOUND.why_the_peer_watch_read_zero: They watched +0x140, which is the HEAL field. Damage was in +0x134 the whole time. My accumulator hypothesis was right in SHAPE and wrong by 12 BYTES.
DAMAGE_FIELD_FOUND.other_drain_caller: Thumb 0x021518D6 passes mov r1,#2; lsl r1,#10 = 2048 raw = 32.0 displayed - a fixed scripted drain, not variable damage.
DAMAGE_FIELD_FOUND.confidence: CONFIRMED_STATIC that 0x020783B8 negates, that 0x0215AC70 calls it, and that the magnitude comes from +0x134 off the same chain. PLAUSIBLE that this is the melee path specifically - it is the right shape, but I have been wrong about shape-being-sufficient once already and the value has not been observed.

THE_REAL_LESSON: I spent five wakes enumerating callers, scanning offsets and building tools, and the pointer I needed was written in docs/research/GDB-Validation-Queue.md by an earlier phase - card 3 note: "a sibling DRAIN trampoline exists at 0x020783B8 (same +0x56c target, negates its delta)". I NEVER READ THE QUEUE BEFORE STARTING THE HUNT. I read Battle-Engine-Map.md (the conclusions) and skipped the document listing what was known-but-unverified. The queue is where a prior campaign parked its LOOSE ENDS, which is exactly what a later campaign needs. Reading conclusions and skipping loose ends is how you re-derive work that was already done.

LOOSE_ENDS_RULE: Both sessions independently made the same mistake this phase: citing GDB-Validation-Queue.md / scripts/gdb/README.md in planning and never reading them, while chasing exactly the thing those documents recorded. K3_RESULT.the_function: 0x02077C0C is the character-init that copies chr_b data into the runtime battle struct.
K3_RESULT.chr_b_lookup_CONFIRMED_IN_CODE: ldr r2,[0x0214BD80]; ldr r2,[r2,#0x0]; ldrb r4,[r1,#0x41] (chr_b index); ldr r12,[r2,#0x40] (table base); mov r2,#0x3C; mla r2,r4,r2,r12. So *(0x0214BD80)+0x40 with stride 0x3C - exactly as the charter described, now confirmed in instructions.
K3_RESULT.THE_DECK_TO_BATTLE_LINK: Battle-struct +0x34 holds a POINTER TO THE PANEL koma.bin RECORD. Its +0x8 (kshapeGroup = size-1) drives every per-size lookup: sub r12,r3,#3 gives size-4, then add r3,r2,r12,lsl #2 and add r12,r2,r12,lsl #1 build two per-size bases (stride 4 and stride 2). That is the whole deck->battle path in three instructions.
K3_RESULT.MY_HP_ARRAY_CONFIRMED_AND_REFINED: The lsl #2 settles the stride question - it IS 4, so the per-size HP array at +0x10 is right. I nearly mis-read this because my add decoder did not print shift fields; without the lsl #2 the code appears to say stride 1, which would make Naruto size-5 HP = 1. BUT the shift also shows my reading was TOO COARSE: +0x10 is an array of five 4-BYTE RECORDS and I had only identified the first byte of each. Record layout: +0x0 max HP (x64), +0x1 REGEN RATE (defaults to 4 if zero), +0x2 unknown, +0x3 unknown.
K3_RESULT.retires_a_loose_end: In iteration 7 I noted that reading those slots as u16 gave "high bytes of 1,4,5,16,20,22" and could not explain it. Those were the REGEN-RATE field of each per-size record. The harness separately measured a live regen rate of 1 - a value from exactly that set.
K3_RESULT.full_copy_map: chr_b[0x00] -> battle +0x13 (BASE NATURE); chr_b[0x01] signed -> +0x11; chr_b[0x02] signed -> +0x10; chr_b[0x10+(size-4)*4] x64 -> +0x16 and +0x18 (max HP, current=max); chr_b[0x11+(size-4)*4] -> +0x49 (regen, default 4); chr_b[0x12+(size-4)*4] -> +0x14; chr_b[0x13+(size-4)*4] -> +0x15; chr_b[0x30] halfword -> +0x2E; chr_b[0x32+(size-4)*2] -> +0x30.
K3_RESULT.two_independent_findings_linked: (1) chr_b[0x00] = base nature (my distribution argument) and nature at runtime +0x13 (harness memory watch) - this instruction is the LINK between those two facts and neither was derived from it. (2) regen at +0x49 (harness watch) is written here at init from a per-size field with a hardcoded default of 4.
K3_RESULT.still_unknown: Four copied fields have no known meaning: chr_b[0x01]/[0x02] -> +0x11/+0x10, and per-size +0x12/+0x13 -> +0x14/+0x15. Plus a per-size HALFWORD array at chr_b[0x32] (stride 2) feeding +0x30, which I had not previously identified at all.
K3_RESULT.caller_unreachable: 0x02077C0C has ZERO direct callers across arm9 and all 14 overlays - dispatched through a pointer table like the other constructors, so whoever supplies the koma record at +0x34 is not statically reachable.

next_leads: Correlate collision subType (+0x01, 16 values) against jpower entry selection - jpower-Mapping.md names this as its own open question ("How do characters select specific jpower entries from their assigned block?") and the collision files are the missing half. Goku has 25 collision records vs 9 jpower block-0 entries: a bounded problem now.

jpower_ID_field: jpower "ID" is a BYTE at record +0x00, confirmed by reproducing the doc block-0 column (0,3,6,9,12,15,18,21,23) exactly. IDs are NOT array indices - entry n has ID 3n for the first seven, then 21 and 23. So "jpower ID" and "jpower entry index" are different numbering, which matters for any lookup.
subType_claim_QUESTIONED: jpower-Mapping.md says "Collision subType selects which jpower entry to use from the block". Now testable with the collision files extracted. Goku (db_b_01, 25 records, chr_b[0] -> block 0 with 9 entries): subType = {0:2, 1:6, 2:13, 5:2, 6:1, 7:1}. Max 7 so it COULD index 9 entries, but 13 of 25 records share subType 2 - a one-to-one move selector would not concentrate half the records on one value. And subType is NOT the jpower ID (block 0 IDs are 0,3,6,...,23 while subTypes include 1,2,5,7). At most a block-relative index. QUESTIONED not refuted - one character tested and the claim may hold for a reading of "entry" I have not guessed. Annotated in the doc.
MY_TYPE_CORRELATION_REFUTED: Reading Goku 25 records I suspected +0x10 was a function of +0x00 (type) - every type-5 record had +0x10=3, every type-3 had 1 or 2. If true, +0x10 would be a derived category and weak as a hitTier candidate. Tested across all 2837 records: types where +0x10 is fully determined = 1 of 8; predicting +0x10 from type alone is right only 50.3% of the time; +0x11 48.7%. Every type spreads across multiple values. THE CORRELATION WAS A 25-RECORD ARTEFACT. So +0x10 (4 values) and +0x11 (7 values) remain INDEPENDENT fields and survive as hitTier/hitProperties candidates - still candidates, not claims. Same failure mode as the chr_b +0x30 over-fit, caught earlier this time because I checked before writing it down.
no_terminator_convention: Goku record 22 is all zeros, which looked like a terminator. Across the whole corpus there is exactly ONE all-zero record - that one. So it is not a convention and code should not treat a zero record as end-of-list.
lessons: LOOSE-ENDS v2 (instance 5, iter 38): grep docs/ AS A WHOLE, for the CONCEPT as well as the filename. I grepped only docs/articles/specs/ and re-derived the already-documented 32-byte shot stride.

READ THE C# SCHEMA FIRST: src/JUS.Tool/Combat/Converters/*.cs are authoritative field-by-field readers. Binary2Collision.cs fixed ProjectileId at 0x03 and named HitTier/HitProperties. 4 of my 5 offset guesses were wrong.

DO NOT bank an untested successor hypothesis (iter 38->39): I refuted the documented ProjectileId reading, proposed "-v-18 into a global 17-entry table" in the same breath, wrote it up as the next lead, and it failed both tests one wake later. Test the successor before recording it as the way forward.

Check for stride arithmetic before calling a field-reading cluster a record walker (iter 40): 11 of 16 collision fields read off one base looked like the parser, but 36 function starts and no #0x14 made it an accessor bank. Caught it myself before writing.

Arity coincidences are not identities (iter 40): 17 spawn kinds vs 17 ProjectileId values is tempting, but only 2 of 17 stubs read the field and their kinds are hardcoded immediates. Declined to claim it.

The ROM has debug symbols and the campaign nearly missed it (iter 41): Battle-Engine-Map claim 7 used BattleAI_* assert strings once, in passing, to identify ov11 - then nobody generalised it for ~30 iterations. When a technique works once, ask what else it names.

Neighbourhood is not containment (iter 41): --nearest gives the closest NAMED function below an address, with unnamed functions in between. Good enough to assign a module (PLAUSIBLE), never enough for CONFIRMED_STATIC.

Shared overlay load addresses bit me a 3rd time (iter 42): 10 overlays share 0x0214CD20, so span-based binary lookup put battle code in Option.cpp/Opening.cpp/Movie.cpp. find_callers.py already warns about exactly this. ANY address->binary lookup in the shared window needs an explicit overlay label.

Quantify a method reach before trusting its output (iter 42): the module map looked like it attributed 177/194 addresses; measuring gap width showed only 43 were trustworthy. The two largest buckets were the two to discard.

Path literals beat .cpp literals for labelling (iter 43): .cpp asserts are ~1 per file (26 refs / 22 files in ov6) so they cannot densify a module map - REFUTED. But a function that loads a file references its path, which identifies purpose directly. That found the collision loader in one pass.

Scanners must stop at function boundaries (iter 44): my char+0x84 -> +0x00 chain scan looked ahead 4 instructions with no boundary check and walked over a bx lr (0xE12FFF1E), inventing a collision-array reader in ov11. With the check, 0 of 10 sites chain. 5th under-constrained-scan false positive this campaign.
x20 stride scanning is not discriminating (iter 44): 70 hits ROM-wide because 20 bytes is a very common struct size. Recognised and abandoned instead of grinding through them.

ACCESSOR-MEDIATED ACCESS is why the walker resisted 40+ iterations (iter 44): the engine never inlines char+0x84 -> prmData+0x00 -> x20. It calls an accessor. Every offset-based search was looking for a chain that does not exist in the instruction stream. Same shape as C3 (Thumb code searched as ARM). Switch to caller-graph search.

AN OFFSET MATCH IS NOT EVIDENCE WITHOUT THE BASE REGISTER TYPE (iter 45): iter 44 called every ldr [Rn,#0x84] a prmData read. The callees index +0x2c/+0x4c, past prmDatas confirmed 0x20 bytes, so those bases are not character structs. Only the STORE at 0x0215F6B0 is confirmed. Cheap fix: trace where the base register came from before believing an offset hit.

WALKER IS STATICALLY UNREACHABLE (iter 45): 4 approaches closed - offset chains (0/10), x20 arithmetic (70 hits), accessor-bank callers (no such bank), stub-bank callers (28/36 zero). Access is assembled at runtime from dispatch-table indices. Needs a harness watchpoint; recipe is in the queue.

ARM BL vs B mask bug (iter 46): (x & 0x0F000000)==0x0A000000 matches B (opcode 0xA) but NEVER BL (0xB). Use 0x0E000000 then test bit 24. My first enumeration silently reported 0 callees for all 73 cases and looked self-consistent; only a previous wake manual disassembly contradicted it.

Shared-command-enum hypothesis REFUTED (iter 46): the 73-way and 13-way ov6 switches both use only low case numbers (13-way live = 1,2,4,6-12), zero overlap with the 73-way no-op band 34-64. Separate enums; the 31-case dead band is unexplained.

B11 dead end recorded (iter 47): dispatcher cases 23/24 call the HP/SP apply functions but NOTHING issues those command numbers. The apply path is reachable a second way that is unused. A handler case existing does not mean it is invoked - enumerate the issuers before building on a case.

ARM mask bug #3 (iter 47): for ldr Rd,[Rn,#imm] I masked the Rn field instead of Rd, so a scan for ldr ip,[Rn,#0x70] returned 0 sites. Correct mask is 0x0FF0FFFF vs 0x0590C070. Added a selftest against a known site before trusting the result - do this every time.
Filter Rn=r15 out of offset scans (iter 47): 14 of 36 ldr [Rn,#0x70] hits were pc-relative literal loads, not field reads at all.

VTABLE SLOT vs STRUCT FIELD (iter 48): before treating ldr Rd,[Rn,#off] as a field read, check whether Rn was just loaded from [Rm,#0]. If so, off is a VTABLE SLOT INDEX and the type is whatever Rm is. ov6 has 384 virtual calls across 33 slots, so this is common, not an edge case. 5th member of the scan-error family: constrain to read every hit / stop at function boundaries / know the base type / exclude r15 bases / check for a preceding vtable load.

Type-verified field mapping works, but needs reassignment tracking (iter 49): anchoring on a known-type register (ldr ip,[rN,#0x70]) is right, but without stopping at writes to rN the scan invented +0x10/+0x28/+0x40/+0x5C AND missed +0x94/+0xa3. The cross-check that proved the fixed version: every constructor store must appear.

RECORDING A RULE DOES NOT APPLY IT (iter 50): iteration 49 found the reassignment-tracking defect and wrote it down; one wake later I wrote a fresh scan without the guard and it reported +0xDF/+0xE0/+0x158 as NoteTrack fields (all beyond its 0xA8 size). Caught only by the size sanity check. The guard must live in a reusable tool, not a note. 6th member of the scan-error family.

Anchor a struct map on the TYPE, not one module (iter 50): iter 49 mapped NoteTrack from BattleNoteTrack.cpp only and missed +0x80/+0x84, which are read by the dispatcher in BattleChara.cpp. Any function that receives the type is a valid anchor.

A guard can be too strict (iter 51): my first ends_block masked off the condition nibble so it stopped at conditional branches (beq is normal in-block flow), finding only 2 of 12 known fields. A missing guard invents fake fields; an over-strict guard loses real ones. Only a selftest with a known-good answer distinguishes them - build the selftest first.

Flag an inconsistency instead of forcing a reading (iter 52): query 71 used stride 0x30 but read +0x158, which cannot both be true of an array of 0x30-byte elements. I recorded it unresolved, then checked how BattleColPrm.cpp used the same global - the base was the MANAGER and the array is embedded at manager+0x158, making both reads land inside one element. The flagged contradiction pointed straight at the correction.

GUARD 5 FALSE POSITIVE (iter 53): ldr Rd,[Rm,#0] is byte-identical for a vtable-pointer load and for dereferencing a singleton global (ldr r0,[pc]=&g; ldr r0,[r0,#0]). The guard suppressed real fields at 7 of 16 ColPrm anchors. Fix: also require a blx/bx on the VALUE the access loads, within 6 instructions. Vtable slots get called; struct fields do not.

A GREEN SELFTEST IS NOT CORRECTNESS (iter 53): the selftest passed both before and after a real tool bug, because its anchors did not exercise the broken path. What caught it was cross-checking the new map against a field known from earlier unrelated work (+0x70 from iter 52). Rule: list a struct known fields BEFORE mapping it, and treat any the tool misses as a tool bug until proven otherwise.

ACCESS COUNT DOES NOT IMPLY HOT STATE (iter 54): I called ColPrm +0xE0/+0xE4/+0xE8 "the per-frame mutable state" because they had 5-6 read+write accesses while other fields were write-once. They are owned sub-object pointers; the reads are a constructor reloading the pointer before each of four setup calls. Construction-via-several-calls and per-frame mutation produce identical access profiles. Read the code before characterising a field.

A FIELD MAPPER CANNOT SEE ARRAYS (iter 55): struct_fields.py reported ColPrm +0x70 and +0xD0 as separate list heads; they are buckets 9 and 21 of a 22-entry array at +0x28. A sparsely-used array always appears as scattered fields. Before reading a map as a struct definition, look for constant strides in the CODE that walks it.

Check whether "table" words decode as instructions (iter 55): I called 0x0207F480/0x0207FB60/0x0207FBB0 handler tables in iteration 54 after printing their words without asking if they were ARM code. All three are functions. One decode step would have caught it.

SCAN BY COMPUTATION SHAPE, NOT OFFSET (iter 56): searching for stores at offsets inside the array range gave 2251 hits ROM-wide; searching for the 0xC0/0x30 stride pair gave 5, of which 4 were the answer. When a structure has distinctive index arithmetic, match the arithmetic - it is orders of magnitude more selective than the offset.

A base inferred from a read offset is under-determined (iter 56): iteration 52 put the array at +0x158 because query 71 two reads had to land in one 0x30 element - true but any base satisfying that fits. The writer computes add r2,sl,#0x154 directly. Prefer a base the CODE computes over one you deduce from a consumer.

ESTABLISH A FUNCTION EXTENT BEFORE NAMING IT (iter 57): I called 0x0207F480 "the per-frame reset" in iteration 55 after reading ~20 of its 440 instructions - it is the collision driver and the drain is only its opening. Same failure as iteration 54 ("handler table" from unread words) and 53 ("hot fields" from access counts): describing a region from the part I happened to print. Finding the next prologue is one step and bounds the thing before you label it.

A zero-write check is also a POSITIVE tool (iter 57): the reassignment guard that caught phantom fields in iterations 49-50 was used here in the affirmative - proving r6 is never written across 440 instructions is what upgraded the writer link to CONFIRMED_STATIC.

UNALIGNED-LOAD TELL (iter 58): a word ldr/str at an offset not divisible by 4 (or ldrh at an odd offset) is a contradiction - no compiler emits it for a struct field. My inline walk (no branch handling) reported 6 offsets off [r6+0x10] including ldr at +0x01/+0x02; the guarded tool gives 2, both ldrsb. Alignment is a free post-hoc validity check on ANY field map.

Two matching byte offsets is not a layout match (iter 58): [r6+0x10] is read at +0x05 and +0x0E, which happen to be CollisionEntry DurationMult and DamageFlags. Declined to claim it - any 20-byte struct has bytes there. Same shape as iteration 50 +0x1a near-miss on prmData.

Check the caller count before reading a function as domain logic (iter 59): 0x0207342C has 303 callers across 10 binaries, which makes it a utility. A high caller count is a cheap signal that a function is library code and its internals will not explain engine behaviour.

Absence of known constants is usable evidence (iter 59): the campaign had already established x5 (jpower damage) and x64 (HP units). Neither appears among 0x020823E4 immediates, which is what let me refute "these are damage figures" rather than leaving it open. Documented magic numbers work as negative tests too.

A once-written register is the strongest anchor there is (iter 60): r8 is written exactly once in 0x020823E4 175 instructions, so every [r8,#imm] in the body is provably a field of that object - no reassignment analysis needed. Worth checking for a single-write register before doing anything more elaborate.

A count matching your expectation is not confirmation (iter 61): my unconstrained scan of stage 1 reported 22 accesses in the bucket byte range, and the array has exactly 22 buckets - so it looked like a clean sweep. With the base register verified the real count is 5; the other 17 reached that numeric range through other registers. The coincidence was what made the contaminated number persuasive.

Report write-counts alongside offset attributions (iter 61): stages 4-7 reassign arg0 3/16/10/24 times, so their bucket attributions are worthless. Counting writes to the base register is a one-line check that tells you whether a whole-function offset scan means anything at all.

Scan the REGISTER LIFETIME, not the function (iter 62): stages 4-7 reassign arg0 3/16/10/24 times, but each reads its bucket within the first 4 instructions. Restricting the walk to entry-until-first-write gave windows of 4/7/2/14 instructions and one clean answer each. Whole-function scanning did not merely add noise - it pointed the wrong way (bucket 7 spurious for two stages).

Do not assume a prologue (iter 62): my walk started at f+4 expecting a push, but stage 6 has no prologue and its ONLY bucket access is the first instruction, so the scan reported "undetermined". Read the actual first instruction rather than skipping an assumed calling convention.

Search the CALLER too, not just the callees you enumerated (iter 63): I scanned stages 1-8 for link calls, found them only in stage 1, and concluded stage 1 was the bucket filler. The driver that CALLS those stages fills ten buckets itself, in a region I had already mislabelled as a reset. When enumerating a set of functions for a behaviour, include the function that dispatches them.

A census is only as wide as its address-recovery (iter 64): iteration 63 resolved link targets only for immediate-offset adds and concluded producers were known for 14 of 22 buckets. Six calls used shifted-register computed bases - exactly how a generic "insert into bucket idx" would be written. The conclusion survived, but by luck. State what forms a census DOES resolve, so the gap is visible.

Run the cheap disconfirming check before publishing a contradiction (iter 64): I drafted "bucket 1 is dead yet the accumulators sit behind it" as an open tension, then ran the obvious escape - does 0x02080F14 walk a live bucket too? It does not (6 of 6 accesses are bucket 1, no computed form). The tension is real, and now it is evidenced rather than asserted.

GREP THE ASSETS YOU BUILT (iter 65): five collision symbols - ColManCreate, ColObjCreate, ColObjAddColWork, ColJointManCreate, ColPrmManCreate - were in jus_files/analysis/symbols.json from iteration 41 and went unread for 24 wakes while I derived the same module structure by hand. The loose-ends rule says grep docs/ before opening a binary; it must also say grep the generated artefacts.

THE LOOSE-ENDS RULE WAS SCOPED TO PROSE (iter 66): "grep docs/ before opening a binary" never covered generated JSON artefacts or an executable query interface, so 25 wakes re-implemented query.py callers / xrefs-to / search-imm / pool-values. Every refinement of the rule stayed inside the same too-narrow search space. Fixed by prior_art.py, which searches artefacts AND prose AND the query CLI in one command.

Prefer the pre-existing tool even when yours works (iter 66): query.py callers found a functions.json caller edge that my find_callers.py structurally cannot see, because mine only scans BL/BLX. A tool I did not write was more complete than the one I built and trusted for 45 wakes.

min(sites)..max(sites) IS NOT A SCOPE (iter 67): I defined "regions where the manager can be in scope" as the span between the first and last global-load site - 0x0207C83C to 0x02157EC8, which covers arm9 AND every overlay. It matched 159 candidates, almost all [sp,#0x30] stack writes. Per-function extents cut it to 1. Same class as iteration 61 "22 accesses in the bucket range": an unconstrained window yielding a plausible count.

State the coverage of a negative, not just its verdict (iter 67): iterations 63-65 concluded "nothing fills buckets 1 and 8" after checking a few hundred instructions, while the complete index shows 499 stores at those offsets ROM-wide. The conclusion held, but I had described a narrow check as if it were exhaustive.

Follow the anomaly in your own data (iter 68): iteration 53 map recorded that +0x18 was the ONLY one of ten init-block words both read and written - the signature of a list head - and I noted it without acting. Fifteen wakes later the complete index proved it. When a map flags one member of a group as behaving differently, that is the thing to chase.

SOME OFFSETS ARE SHARED BY DESIGN (iter 69): +0x08/+0x10/+0x18/+0x20 are this codebase conventional list-head offsets, recurring on four different object types. Of 21 link/unlink sites at +0x18/+0x20 only ONE verified as the ColPrm manager. This is stronger than "check the base register" - for conventional offsets the offset itself carries no information at all, so base verification is not a guard but the entire measurement.

The offset-collision hazard is quantified (iter 70): 2 of the 8 unlink sites at +0x18 belong to the COLJOINT manager, not ColPrm. Matching on offset alone would have tripled the apparent pool traffic and shown allocations that never happen. Iteration 69 caution about +0x08/+0x10 was also vindicated - the allocator links into r4+8 where r4 is the OWNER.

Locating is not naming (iter 71): the task was "identify the owner" and I finished with [ColObj+0x28] - a precise address expression, not an identity. Worth labelling the difference in the writeup rather than letting a location read as an answer.

When two hops in a row fail to name a thing, change method (iter 72): iterations 71 and 72 each moved the owner pointer one dereference closer and neither produced an identity - the address expression got longer, not shorter. Name it from the object shape (size + field pattern cross-checked against known constructors), which is how ColObj 0x40 and ColWork 0x64 were identified.

A failed heredoc assertion does not stop a following git commit (iter 72): my map edit asserted on a stale anchor and died, but the next command still committed - so the doc landed without the map or state updates. When a commit is chained after a scripted edit, verify the edit succeeded before committing, or make them one command.

THE PRIOR-ART GATE MUST FIRE BEFORE WRITING THE DOC, NOT ONLY BEFORE STARTING WORK. Iteration 73 had a doc written AND edit-passed claiming 'the battle character struct is 0x1F0 bytes -- CONFIRMED_STATIC' when Battle-Engine-Map.md had recorded 0x02156A58 / 0x1F0 = 496 bytes since an earlier campaign. One grep of docs/ for the headline address would have caught it. New hard rule: grep docs/ for every address in a doc's headline claim before writing the doc.

'ALL KNOWN OFFSETS FIT INSIDE THE SIZE' IS NOT A CROSS-CHECK when the offsets were harvested from more than one object. Five offsets all landing below 0x1F0 is exactly what you expect if some belong to a 0x1F0 object and some to a 0x570 one. It proves nothing about either.

THE ALLOCATOR IS TAGGED -- USE IT INSTEAD OF NEAREST-FUNCTION BINDING. 0x0201A21C takes the .cpp name and function name as arguments, so a size binds to a NAME AT THE CALL SITE. That is strictly stronger than extract_symbols.py, which can only say a string sits near some code. 469 of 494 sites resolve. Every earlier nearest-bind attribution is now re-checkable.

A LONG-STANDING LABEL CAN BE THE BUG. 'MoveInfo' for [char+0x1a8] survived several campaigns and shaped the damage-pipeline claims; it was wrong. When two documented facts about one object refuse to reconcile (a 0x1F0 allocation vs a +0x56c field), suspect the naming before inventing an indirection.

AN ABSENCE IN THE CENSUS IS EVIDENCE. No battle allocation >=0x570 among 431 sized sites means the outer object is not heap-allocated through this allocator -- a real structural fact from a negative result, provided the census width (431 of 494, 63 computed and excluded) is stated.

A TWO-ARGUMENT STORE TELLS YOU NOTHING ABOUT WHICH ARGUMENT IS THE CONTAINER. Iteration 73 read 'mov r4,r1 / str r0,[r4,#0x1a8]' and assigned the roles by assumption, getting them exactly backwards and inventing a >=0x570 outer object that does not exist. xrefs-to returned ONE reference and settled it in a minute. Always find a caller before naming roles.

ZERO CALLERS MEANS CALLBACK, AND THE INVOKER SUPPLIES THE ROLES. Twice now (0x0207D440 in iteration 71, 0x021570EC here) a function with no callers turned out to be a function pointer. The right move is xrefs-to for a literal load, then read the blx site -- not to guess the signature from the body.

AN 'IMPOSSIBLE' SIZE CONFLICT IS USUALLY TWO OBJECTS, NOT A WRAPPER. A 0x1F0 allocation and a +0x56c field cannot be one struct. Iteration 73 resolved that by inventing an outer container; the truth was two separate structs in two separate binaries (ov6 battle character, arm9 +0x56c struct). Prefer 'these are different objects' over 'there is a hidden layer'.

A CORRECTION CAN BE THE MOST VALUABLE WAKE. Iteration 74 produced no new subsystem, but it reversed a wrong claim before it propagated into the map's damage-pipeline reasoning AND yielded the character<->entity bidirectional link as a by-product. Re-deriving a suspect claim is real work, not overhead.

READ THE RETURN VALUE BEFORE FOLLOWING ANOTHER POINTER. Iterations 71-73 chased the owner outward through three correct pointer hops and never asked what installer 0x0207C988 RETURNS -- one instruction (mov r0,r4 at 0x0207CB34) that named it outright. A return value is a stronger handle on an object's identity than any field.

A PARKED QUESTION CAN BE ANSWERED BY A DIFFERENT THREAD. The pool-node owner was parked at iteration 73 after three failed wakes; iteration 75 settled it as a side effect of resolving an unrelated contradiction. Parking is the right call, but re-check parked items against every new structural result rather than treating them as closed.

A CONTRADICTION BETWEEN TWO WAKES IS A HIGH-YIELD TASK, NOT A CHORE. 'entity+0x10 is the ColObj' vs 'entity+0x10 is the damage scratch object' looked like a bookkeeping fix. Settling it refuted one claim, unified three objects, answered a parked question, and sharpened the campaign's top open item (B11).

IF THE SEARCH SPACE CANNOT CONTAIN THE ANSWER, THE METHOD IS WRONG NO MATTER HOW WELL IT RUNS. Iteration 73 matched the owner's >=0x183 size against the tagged-allocation census; the owner is pool-allocated and was never on that list. Before running a census-style search, check that the target could appear in it at all.

AN EXHAUSTIVE NEGATIVE IS A RESULT -- BUT ONLY IF ITS BLIND SPOTS ARE COUNTED. '0 writers found' means nothing without the denominator. find_field_writers.py prints thumb-function counts, stm counts and register-offset-store counts on every run, so a zero can never be read as proof. ov6 being only 2% thumb with 13 reg-offset stores is what makes this particular zero meaningful.

EXCLUDE CONVENTIONAL OFFSETS FROM A COMPANION LIST OR IT MATCHES EVERYTHING. Including +0x8 gave 7 'MATCH' sites; dropping it (iteration 69 established it as a shared list-head offset) gave 0. A discriminator built from common offsets is not a discriminator.

TEST THE SUCCESSOR IN THE SAME WAKE, AS THE CHARTER SAYS. The owner+0xA4 sub-region hypothesis was well-motivated (0xA4+0x44=0xE8, and the installer memsets from there) and took one query to refute: ov6 has 0 `add rX,rY,#0xa4` sites. Recorded as REFUTED instead of banked as next wake's lead.

WHEN A FIELD HAS NO WRITER, CONSIDER THAT IT HAS NO WRITER. Four rounds assumed the +0xE8 writer was hiding. The convergent evidence -- no store ROM-wide, zeroed at install, and a sibling field observed as 0 at a live breakpoint -- points at a vestigial field and a dead read. Reframing beats a fifth search round.

ASK WHAT MEMSETS AN OBJECT TO SIZE IT. Four wakes chased the owner through pointer hops and allocation-size matching and never sized it. One block-write sweep found the teardown's `memset(record, 0, 0x188)` -- the object's size, its free-pool destination and its manager all in five instructions. A destructor is as informative as a constructor and is often easier to find.

FINGERPRINT A STRUCT BY A DISTINCTIVE MULTI-FIELD SHAPE, NOT ONE OFFSET. Confirming r5 was the ColPrm manager came from the +0xFC/+0x100/+0x104 phase-table dispatch, a shape nothing else in the ROM has. Single-offset matching failed 20 of 21 times at iteration 69; a three-field consecutive dispatch is unambiguous.

CLOSING A BLIND SPOT CAN PAY MORE THAN THE QUESTION THAT OPENED IT. The block sweep was queued to finish B11 and added nothing to B11 -- but it named and sized the most load-bearing struct in the combat engine. Finish the sweep you started; the by-catch is often the point.

STATE THE EXCLUDED COUNT EVERY TIME. The block pass resolved 5 covering calls and excluded 124 with computed destinations or sizes. Reporting '5 sites' without the 124 would read as exhaustive when it covers a minority of call sites.

A LOAD/STORE-ONLY SCAN CANNOT SEE STRUCTURAL FIELDS. Every list head and every embedded sub-region in this codebase is reached by `add rD,base,#imm` and then passed to a call -- never as `[base,#imm]`. struct_fields.py had six guards and still missed +0x08, +0x90, +0x94 and +0xA4 on the ColPrm record, i.e. exactly the fields that define its shape. Address-taken is a field reference.

A SPLIT BASE IS NOT A FIELD. `add r0,r4,#0x100` followed by `strh r2,[r0,#0x86]` means +0x186; reporting +0x100 would invent a field and hide a real one. ARM's 12-bit immediate reaches 0x186 directly, so this is a compiler choice that shows up on this codebase's larger structs -- resolve it, do not record it.

CROSS-BINARY AGREEMENT ON ONE FIELD BEATS ANOTHER POINTER HOP. That arm9's installer and ov6's damage path both touch +0x40 on the same struct is independent support for an identity that had rested purely on an address expression since iteration 75. Look for two binaries reaching one field before adding another indirection.

A FIELD MAP IS ONLY AS WIDE AS ITS ANCHORS -- SAY SO. 24 fields on a 0x188 struct from six anchor functions is a partial map. Publishing it without the unmapped spans listed would read as the struct's definition and get cited as one.

POST-INDEXED ADDRESSING IS INVISIBLE TO OFFSET SCANS, AND THAT IS WHERE ARRAY WALKS LIVE. `strh r2,[r5],#2` has no immediate to match, so every scanner in this repo skips it silently. Iteration 79 could not find a single reader of three arrays precisely because the code that walks them uses this form. Count it and state it like the stm and Thumb blind spots.
